verdict.rationale: Windows' own marketing pages say users can organize windows on screen with Snap layouts and create Snap groups to return to, which directly matches snapping and tiling windows into predefined layouts for multitasking. The evidence is marketing-level only, with no detailed documentation of layout options, keyboard or drag behavior, or multi-monitor handling. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party how-to documentation of the available layouts and controls, independent or hands-on corroboration that Snap layouts work well in practice.
